title: Air-Fryer Chicken Wings
subtitle: Crispy chicken wings with no frying and very little oil
excerpt: Chicken wings tossed with baking powder, salt, and spices and cooked in the air fryer until the skin is extraordinarily crisp. The baking powder trick makes them crispier than deep-fried.

recipe.sourceNotes: The baking powder trick for crispy wings was popularised by J. Kenji Lopez-Alt and works because the alkaline baking powder raises the pH of the chicken skin, which causes it to brown and crisp more readily during cooking. The effect is dramatically amplified when combined with an air fryer. Use aluminium-free baking powder to avoid any metallic taste. The wings can be dressed with any sauce after cooking.

content.text: Dry the wings before seasoning: moisture is the enemy of crisp skin. Flip the wings halfway through cooking to crisp both sides. The wings can be tossed in sauce immediately after cooking: the crisp skin absorbs a little sauce but stays crunchy for 5 to 10 minutes.

items.preparation: tips removed if whole, patted dry

content.text: Pat the wings completely dry with kitchen paper. Mix the baking powder, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper together. Toss the wings with the spice mix until evenly coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 C for 3 minutes. Arrange the wings in a single layer in the basket, skin-side up. Do not crowd them.
Cook at 200 C for 12 minutes. Flip the wings and cook for a further 10 to 13 minutes until the skin is deeply golden and crackling-crisp.
Serve plain or toss immediately in your chosen sauce. Buffalo sauce, barbecue sauce, or a honey and soy glaze all work well.
